# PRACTICE DIRECTION 42 – CHANGE OF SOLICITOR

## This Practice Direction supplements Part 42 of the Civil Procedure Rules

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 42 – CHANGE OF SOLICITOR > This Practice Direction supplements Part 42 of the Civil Procedure Rules] Contents of this Practice Direction

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 42 – CHANGE OF SOLICITOR > This Practice Direction supplements Part 42 of the Civil Procedure Rules] Title

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 42 – CHANGE OF SOLICITOR > This Practice Direction supplements Part 42 of the Civil Procedure Rules] Solicitor acting for a party

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 42 – CHANGE OF SOLICITOR > This Practice Direction supplements Part 42 of the Civil Procedure Rules] Notice of change of solicitor

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 42 – CHANGE OF SOLICITOR > This Practice Direction supplements Part 42 of the Civil Procedure Rules] Application for an order that a solicitor has ceased to act

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 42 – CHANGE OF SOLICITOR > This Practice Direction supplements Part 42 of the Civil Procedure Rules] Application by another party to remove a solicitor

## Solicitor acting for a party

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 42 – CHANGE OF SOLICITOR > Solicitor acting for a party] 1.1 Rule 42.1 states that where the address for service of a party is the business address 1 of that party’s solicitor, the solicitor will be considered to be acting for that party until the provisions of Part 42 have been complied with.

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 42 – CHANGE OF SOLICITOR > Solicitor acting for a party] 1.2 Subject to rule 42.2(6) (where the certificate of a LSC funded client or assisted person is revoked or discharged), where a party has changed his solicitor or intends to act in person, the former solicitor will be considered to be the party’s solicitor unless or until;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 42 – CHANGE OF SOLICITOR > Solicitor acting for a party] (1) a notice of the change is

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 42 – CHANGE OF SOLICITOR > Solicitor acting for a party] (a) filed with the court 2 , and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 42 – CHANGE OF SOLICITOR > Solicitor acting for a party] (b) served on every other party 3 , or

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 42 – CHANGE OF SOLICITOR > Solicitor acting for a party] (2) the court makes an order under rule 42.3 and the order is served on every other party 4 .

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 42 – CHANGE OF SOLICITOR > Solicitor acting for a party] The notice should not be filed until every other party has been served.

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 42 – CHANGE OF SOLICITOR > Solicitor acting for a party] 1.3 A solicitor appointed to represent a party only as an advocate at a hearing will not be considered to be acting for that party within the meaning of Part 42.

## Notice of change of solicitor

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 42 – CHANGE OF SOLICITOR > Notice of change of solicitor] 2.1 Rule 42.2(1) sets out the circumstances following which a notice of the change must be filed and served.

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 42 – CHANGE OF SOLICITOR > Notice of change of solicitor] 2.2 A notice of the change giving the last known address of the former assisted person must also be filed and served on every party where, under rule 42.2(6):

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 42 – CHANGE OF SOLICITOR > Notice of change of solicitor] (1) the certificate of a LSC funded client or assisted person is revoked or discharged,

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 42 – CHANGE OF SOLICITOR > Notice of change of solicitor] (2) the solicitor who acted for that person ceased to act on determination of his retainer under regulation 83 of those Regulations, and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 42 – CHANGE OF SOLICITOR > Notice of change of solicitor] (3) the LSC funded client or the assisted person wishes either to act in person or appoint another solicitor to act on his behalf.

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 42 – CHANGE OF SOLICITOR > Notice of change of solicitor] 2.3 In addition, where a party or solicitor changes his address for service, a notice of that change should be filed and served on every party.

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 42 – CHANGE OF SOLICITOR > Notice of change of solicitor] 2.4 A party who, having conducted a claim by a solicitor, intends to act in person must give in the notice an address for service that is within the United Kingdom 5 .

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 42 – CHANGE OF SOLICITOR > Notice of change of solicitor] 2.5 Subject to paragraph 2.7A, practice form N434 should be used to give notice of any change. The notice should be filed in the court office in which the claim is proceeding.

## 2.6 Omitted

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 42 – CHANGE OF SOLICITOR > 2.6 Omitted] 2.7 Subject to paragraph 2.7A, where the claim is the subject of an appeal to the Court of Appeal, the notice should also be filed in the Civil Appeals Office.

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 42 – CHANGE OF SOLICITOR > 2.6 Omitted] 2.7A If notice of change is being given by a solicitor who has a MyHMCTS account, and that solicitor will be conducting the claim to which the notice of change relates through their MyHMCTS account, the solicitor should not use practice form N434, but instead should file notice of change with the court using MyHMCTS.

## Application for an order that a solicitor has ceased to act

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 42 – CHANGE OF SOLICITOR > Application for an order that a solicitor has ceased to act] 3.1 A solicitor may apply under rule 42.3 for an order declaring that he has ceased to be the solicitor acting for a party.

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 42 – CHANGE OF SOLICITOR > Application for an order that a solicitor has ceased to act] 3.2 The application should be made in accordance with Part 23 6 and must be supported by evidence 7 . Unless the court directs otherwise the application notice must be served on the party 8 .

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 42 – CHANGE OF SOLICITOR > Application for an order that a solicitor has ceased to act] 3.3 An order made under rule 42.3 must be served on every party and takes effect when it is served. Where the order is not served by the court, the person serving must file a certificate of service in practice form N215.

## Application by another party to remove a solicitor

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 42 – CHANGE OF SOLICITOR > Application by another party to remove a solicitor] 4.1 Rule 42.4 sets out circumstances in which any other party may apply for an order declaring that a solicitor has ceased to be the solicitor acting for another party in the proceedings.

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 42 – CHANGE OF SOLICITOR > Application by another party to remove a solicitor] 4.2 The application should be made in accordance with Part 23 and must be supported by evidence. Unless the court directs otherwise the application notice must be served on the party to whose solicitor the application relates.

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 42 – CHANGE OF SOLICITOR > Application by another party to remove a solicitor] 4.3 An order made under rule 42.4 must be served on every other party to the proceedings. Where the order is not served by the court, the person serving must file a certificate of service in practice form N215.

## New address for service where order made under rules 42.3 or 42.4

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 42 – CHANGE OF SOLICITOR > New address for service where order made under rules 42.3 or 42.4] 5.1 Where the court has made an order under rule 42.3 that a solicitor has ceased to act or under rule 42.4 declaring that a solicitor has ceased to be the solicitor for a party, the party for whom the solicitor was acting must give a new address for service to comply with rules 6.23(1) and 6.24.

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 42 – CHANGE OF SOLICITOR > New address for service where order made under rules 42.3 or 42.4] (Rule 6.23(2)(a) provides that a party must give an address for service within the United Kingdom or where a solicitor is acting for a party, an address for service either in the United Kingdom or any other EEA state.)

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 42 – CHANGE OF SOLICITOR > New address for service where order made under rules 42.3 or 42.4] (Until such time as a new address for service is given rule 6.9 will apply.)
